title: Attention kernel profiling: FlashAttention / paged / fused runbook
content:
Summary:
This runbook collects the experimental setup, profiling outputs, bottleneck analysis, and recommended next steps for attention-kernel optimizations we evaluated between FlashAttention, paged-attention, and fused QKV/softmax ops. The goal is to converge on a default runtime path (and fallbacks) for v1.3 of the serving runtime to improve p50/p90 generation latency while preserving throughput and memory headroom.

High-level findings (short):
- FlashAttention (v2-style kernels) gives the best latency for medium-length sequences (<= 4k) when tensors fit in GPU memory and when KV-cache reuse is minimal.
- Paged attention enables stable memory usage and better tail latency for long sequences (>4k) at the cost of some extra kernel launches and modest throughput reduction.
- Fused QKV + fused softmax + fused dropout ops reduce CPU-GPU syncs and operator overhead, improving throughput for small batch sizes (B<=8) but are sensitive to layout and quantization.
- Best overall: a routing policy that prefers FlashAttention for short/medium context, paged-attention for long-context requests, and enables fused ops for request types with small batch sizes and high concurrency.

Goals of experiments:
- Measure p50/p90 token-generation latency and tokens/sec for representative workloads.
- Identify kernel-level bottlenecks using Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute.
- Understand memory behavior (peak alloc, fragmentation) across attention implementations.
- Produce concrete runtime heuristics (sequence-length and batch-size thresholds) for automatic routing.

Experimental setup:
- Code branch: profiling/attention-opt (PR: linked above).
- Models: Llama2-13B (float16), Mistral-7B baseline (float16) for small-model comparisons.
- Hardware: AWS p4d.24xlarge (8x A100 40GB) for distributed runs; single-GPU experiments on a single A100-40GB node.
- Framework: PyTorch 2.2 + Triton kernels where applicable. FlashAttention kernels pulled from third_party/flashattention@v2.1.
- Metrics: p50/p90 generation latency per token (ms), decoded tokens/sec, GPU utilization (nvidia-smi), GPU memory peak, kernel time breakdown (Nsight Compute).
- Synthetic prompts: short (64 tokens), medium (1024), long (4096, 8192) with both random and realistic prefix distributions.
- Batch sizes tested: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16; temperature=1.0, max_new_tokens tuned to 512 for stability.

Representative results (single-GPU, Llama2-13B, fp16, KV-cache cold -> un-cached streaming generation):
- Short (64):
  - Baseline (naive attention): p50=7.8ms, p90=12.4ms, tokens/sec=770
  - FlashAttention: p50=5.0ms, p90=8.1ms, tokens/sec=1200
  - Fused ops + FlashAttention: p50=4.6ms, p90=7.5ms, tokens/sec=1300
- Medium (1024):
  - Baseline: p50=18.2ms, p90=35.0ms, tokens/sec=450
  - FlashAttention: p50=12.0ms, p90=20.5ms, tokens/sec=740
  - Paged attention: p50=13.5ms, p90=21.8ms, tokens/sec=700 (peak mem reduced by ~22%)
- Long (4096):
  - Baseline: OOM or extremely slow due to memory copies
  - FlashAttention: p50=48ms, p90=120ms, tokens/sec=180 (mem pressure high, fragmentation observed)
  - Paged attention: p50=40ms, p90=70ms, tokens/sec=240 (more stable tail, lower peak mem)

Profiling notes (Nsight Compute / triton):
- FlashAttention: kernel time dominated by single large matmul-like kernel. Good occupancy when sequence length has even multiples for block sizes; performance drops for odd or small sequence partitions. Kernel launch overhead low.
- Paged attention: multiple smaller kernels per layer (page load, local attention, KV writeback). Increased kernel launch counts -> more context switch overhead, but each kernel is smaller and fits L2/cache better.
- Fused QKV: reduces separate GEMM launches for q/k/v -> measurably lowers CPU prep time and PCIe syncs for small batches. When fused, we saw CPU-side scheduling reduced by ~12% in profiler traces.
- Memory: fragmentation occurred with FlashAttention when dynamic allocation pattern matched model used + varying sequence lengths. Paged attention enforced stable allocations per-page which reduced fragmentation and peak allocations.

Bottleneck analysis (layer-by-layer):
- Early layers: compute-bound (matmul/attn kernels). FlashAttention wins.
- Middle layers: memory-bound when using KV-cache heavily (read/write throughput). Paged attention reduces cache pressure.
- Late layers / output: small GEMMs and softmax become significant for small batch sizes — fused-softmax reduces kernel counts and improves throughput.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Quantized models (int8/4-bit): Fused kernels sometimes break assumptions about layouts -> incorrect outputs in some cases (we tracked two bugs tied to row-major vs col-major layout expectations). Tests added in PR to catch layout mismatch.
- Multi-GPU sharded KV-cache: paged-attention requires careful coordination to avoid cross-device page thrash. Current implementation uses a centralized page directory; this needs locking improvements under high concurrency.
- Cold KV-cache vs warm cache: flashattention wins on cold-start single-token latency; paged-attention often better when cache is warm and long-context reuse occurs.

Heuristics (proposal for runtime):
- If seq_len <= 2048 and estimated GPU memory headroom >= 2GB: prefer FlashAttention + fused ops (if fused kernels pass shape/layout checks).
- If seq_len > 2048 or estimated peak allocation > available_headroom: route to paged-attention.
- If batch_size <= 8 and concurrency high: enable fused QKV + fused softmax to reduce kernel overhead.
- Maintain an automatic guardrail: if FlashAttention path triggers >3 OOMs in last 10k requests, automatically switch to paged-attention for that model/version until restart or manual override.

Recommended runtime changes (short-term):
1) Enable fused-QKV for small-batch routes behind an opt-in flag and add strict layout checks (owner: Asha Patel, RFC linked).
2) Add paged-attention as a compiled alternative with a sequence-length threshold and memory-estimation fallback (owner: Evan Chen).
3) Integrate Nsight-lite traces into nightly performance-ci for the serving runtime to catch regressions in kernel times (owner: Daniel Kim).
4) Add unit+integration tests for quantized fused-kernels (owner: María López).

Action items and owners:
- Asha: push fused-QKV PR changes + add layout validation hooks (due 2026-02-28).
- Evan: improve page-directory locking and add stress test for multi-GPU page thrash (due 2026-03-10).
- Daniel: add perf-ci job and baseline traces for current master (due 2026-03-05).
- María: add quantization regression tests and integrate into CI (due 2026-03-01).

Open questions / research spikes:
- Can we design a hybrid kernel that adapts at runtime between Flash-like large-kernel and paged micro-kernel depending on sequence alignment? (Spike: 2 engineer-weeks).
- What are TLX costs of enabling fused ops across all model families — i.e., maintenance burden and probability of accidental correctness breaks for future quant formats?
- Can we simulataneously reduce kernel-launch overhead for paged attention by batching page kernels across layers? (prototype idea exists, needs benchmarking).

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducing experiments locally
- Clone branch profiling/attention-opt and install triton, torch pinned to 2.2.
- Export MODEL=llama2-13b; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0; run tools/run_attention_bench.py --seq-lens 64 1024 4096 --batches 1 4 8 --backend flash,paged,fused --warmup 20 --steps 200
- Collect traces: NSYS_OUTPUT=trace.nsys python tools/run_attention_bench.py ... ; then ncu --import trace.nsys --target-processes all

Notes to reviewers:
- Numbers above are representative from single-node experiments and tuned kernels; real multi-tenant hosted results will vary. The routing heuristics are conservative by design.
- Please review the heuristic thresholds and the OOM-guard rule; we want to avoid oscillation in routing under bursty traffic.

Thread links / context: the runbook collates prior notes (see sibling docs in this folder). This is intended to be the canonical doc for the team to implement runtime heuristic changes in v1.3.
